newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan October consumer prices up 3.69 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan October consumer prices up 3.69 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's consumer prices in October rose 3.69 percent from a year earlier, the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics said on Tuesday.
On a month-to-month basis, the October consumer price index was down 0.39 percent from September, the directorate said.
At the wholesale level, October wholesale prices were down 2.23 percent from October 1995 and down 0.63 percent from September 1996.
Consumer prices have risen an aggregate 3.12 percent during the first 10 months of 1996, well within the government's second-half target of 3.5 percent, the agency said.
The agency gave no new forecast for full-year inflation. Its last forecast, issued in August, said prices were on course to rise 3.33 percent for the entire calendar year.

The statistical agency's director, Chan Teh-sung, gave three reasons for what he called October's "stable consumer prices": stable international consumer prices, slow growth of domestic salaries and an overall slow domestic economy.
Chan noted that wholesale prices had registered a year-on-year decline for the seventh consecutive month.

The directorate said that food prices overall had fallen 1.65 percent from September, indicating that the economy was still recovering from a spate of summer typhoons that wrecked crops and sent food prices soaring in June, July and August.
Electricity prices also fell in October with the passage of summer and the peak air-conditioning season, it said.
Hotel prices registered a downturn, it said.
